A reservation management device is configured to manage reservations for exchanging battery packs at a charging device. The charging device may be used to receive depleted or partially depleted battery packs from users and provide charged battery packs in exchange. In order to manage this exchange efficiently, the reservation management device determines whether a requested battery pack exchange can be reserved in advance.

The reservation management device includes a reservation number acquisition component, a return number acquisition component, and a reservation possibility determination component.

The reservation number acquisition component obtains information indicating the number of battery packs to be reserved at the charging device. This number may correspond to the quantity of charged battery packs requested by a user for a planned exchange.

The return number acquisition component obtains information indicating the number of battery packs to be returned to the charging device. This number may correspond to the quantity of battery packs that the user is expected to bring back to the charging device during the exchange.

The reservation possibility determination component determines whether a reservation for battery pack exchange can be accepted. This determination is made based on the number of battery packs to be reserved and the number of battery packs to be returned. By considering both the outgoing battery packs and the incoming battery packs, the reservation management device can more accurately manage the availability of battery packs at the charging device and decide whether the requested exchange can be reserved.

A reservation management device is provided for managing reservations for exchanging battery packs at a charging device, such as a battery swap station. The charging device stores and charges a plurality of battery packs and supplies charged battery packs to users who have made exchange reservations. When a user requests an exchange reservation, the reservation management device acquires information indicating the number of battery packs requested by the user for reservation. In addition, the reservation management device acquires information indicating the number of battery packs expected to be returned to the charging device, for example, battery packs that users are scheduled to bring back at the time of exchange.

Based on both the number of battery packs requested for reservation and the number of battery packs expected to be returned, the reservation management device determines whether the requested exchange reservation can be accepted. For instance, even if the current number of available charged battery packs is insufficient, the device may determine that the reservation is possible when enough battery packs are expected to be returned and charged before the scheduled exchange time. Conversely, the device may refuse or adjust the reservation if the number of requested battery packs exceeds the number that can be reliably supplied after taking expected returns into account.

By considering not only the present inventory of charged battery packs but also the expected inflow of returned battery packs, the reservation management device can more accurately determine battery pack availability. This improves the reliability of exchange reservations, reduces the likelihood of accepting reservations that cannot be fulfilled, and enables more efficient operation of the charging device. As a result, users can reserve battery pack exchanges with greater confidence, while operators can better manage battery pack inventory, charging schedules, and overall station availability.

**The**

“The” is one of the smallest words in the English language, yet it is also one of the most important. It appears everywhere: in books, conversations, songs, news, and everyday speech. Although it seems simple, “the” helps make meaning clear. It points to something specific, something known, or something already mentioned.

For example, when we say “a book,” we could mean any book. But when we say “the book,” we mean a particular book that the listener can identify. This small word gives direction and focus to a sentence. It helps connect ideas and makes communication smoother.

“The” is called a definite article. It shows that a noun is not general, but specific. We use it when talking about unique things, such as “the sun,” “the moon,” or “the sky.” We also use it when referring to something familiar, like “the teacher,” “the house,” or “the story.”

Even though “the” is short, it plays a powerful role in language. Without it, many sentences would sound incomplete or unclear. It reminds us that sometimes the smallest words can have the greatest importance.

counterfactuals.output: A reservation management device for a charging station at which battery packs are exchanged includes a control unit configured to manage reservations for battery-pack exchange. The control unit acquires a reserved battery quantity corresponding to a number of battery packs reserved for exchange during a predetermined time period, and acquires a returned battery quantity corresponding to a number of battery packs expected or scheduled to be returned to the charging station during the predetermined time period. The control unit determines reservation availability for an additional battery-pack exchange reservation based on the reserved battery quantity and the returned battery quantity. In this manner, the device enables reservation acceptance that reflects both demand for battery packs and replenishment of battery packs at the charging station.

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a formal technical description of an invention where a device manages battery swap reservations by comparing the number of battery packs reserved with the number expected to be returned.
counterfactuals.output:
A battery swap reservation management device is provided for controlling acceptance of reservations at a battery exchange facility. The device includes a communication interface, a memory, and one or more processors configured to execute reservation management logic.

The communication interface receives reservation requests from user terminals, vehicle-mounted devices, or an external service server. Each reservation request may include at least one of a desired battery swap time, a battery type, a quantity of battery packs to be received by a user, a quantity of depleted or partially depleted battery packs to be returned by the user, and identification information for the user or vehicle.

The memory stores reservation information indicating battery packs already reserved for delivery during one or more future time periods. The memory also stores return forecast information indicating battery packs expected to be returned to the battery exchange facility during the same or corresponding future time periods. The return forecast information may be generated from existing reservations, historical return data, vehicle usage data, battery state-of-charge information, user schedules, or communications from users who intend to return battery packs.

The processor determines, for a target reservation period, a reserved battery quantity representing the number of battery packs already reserved for withdrawal from the facility. The processor further determines an expected return quantity representing the number of battery packs expected to be returned to the facility during or before the target reservation period. The processor compares the reserved battery quantity with the expected return quantity to determine whether accepting a new reservation would cause an imbalance between battery pack demand and battery pack availability.

In one implementation, when the number of battery packs reserved, including the requested quantity in a new reservation request, is less than or equal to the number of battery packs expected to be returned, the processor accepts the reservation and stores corresponding reservation data in the memory. When the number of battery packs reserved exceeds the number of battery packs expected to be returned, the processor rejects the reservation, places the reservation on a waiting list, proposes an alternative reservation time, or limits the number of battery packs available for reservation.

The device may also take into account a current inventory quantity of charged battery packs at the facility, a charging completion forecast for battery packs currently being charged, a minimum reserve threshold, battery pack type compatibility, battery health status, or priority information associated with particular users. In such an embodiment, the processor determines an available future battery quantity based on at least the current charged inventory, expected returned battery packs, and expected charging completions, and compares the available future battery quantity with the reserved battery quantity. Reservations are accepted only when the available future battery quantity satisfies a predetermined availability condition.

The device may update the comparison dynamically as new reservations are received, as users cancel reservations, as battery packs are actually returned, or as charging status changes. The processor may transmit reservation confirmation, rejection, or modification information to the user terminal or vehicle-mounted device through the communication interface.

Accordingly, the invention enables a battery swap facility to manage future battery availability by coordinating outgoing reserved battery packs with incoming returned battery packs. This reduces overbooking, improves battery inventory reliability, and allows reservation acceptance to be controlled based on predicted replenishment of battery packs.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3
